title: Benefits Verification Bulletin: Insulin Record and Medicare Coverage Risk for Sensors, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
### Benefits Verification Bulletin

**Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program — CGM Original Medicare Program.** Which of the units listed on a customer's Medicare advance beneficiary notice (form CMS-R-131) for the CGM supply allowance (item A4239) Medicare is expected to deny follows the customer's insulin record. The insulin record is read from the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program: the program's status, its closure reason, and the ship date and supply days of its insulin refill shipments.

**Expected denial.** This bulletin replaces the expectation that Medicare pays every listed unit: when the customer has stopped insulin and the latest insulin refill's supply on the customer's insulin pharmacy program, its ship date plus its supply days, ends before the next delivery date, an insulin pharmacy program with no insulin refill on record counting as a supply that ended before it, Medicare is expected to deny every listed unit; when the customer has stopped insulin but that supply still runs on or after the next delivery date, it is expected to deny the listed units less one 30-day block's allowance, never fewer than zero; otherwise the standard expectation applies, Medicare being expected to pay every listed unit and to deny none.

- The insulin record shows the customer has stopped insulin only when the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is closed with closure reason "customer discontinued". A closed insulin pharmacy program with closure reason "changed supplier", or any other reason, and an insulin pharmacy program that is active, on hold or not yet active, fall under the last branch.
- The *latest insulin refill* is the insulin refill shipment on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program with the latest ship date; its supply ends on its ship date plus its supply days, in calendar days. A program closed with closure reason "customer discontinued" that has no insulin refill shipment on record is read as a supply that ended before the next delivery date.
- *One 30-day block's allowance* is the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply; the units expected to be denied under the second branch are never fewer than zero.

| Insulin pharmacy program | Latest insulin refill supply, against the next delivery date | Units Medicare is expected to deny |
|---|---|---|
| Closed, closure reason "customer discontinued" | Ends earlier than the next delivery date | Every listed unit |
| Closed, closure reason "customer discontinued" | No insulin refill on record | Every listed unit |
| Closed, closure reason "customer discontinued" | Runs on the next delivery date or later | The listed units less one 30-day block's allowance, not below zero |
| Any other status or closure reason | — | None: Medicare is expected to pay every listed unit |

**Verification examples (hypothetical figures).** Suppose the notice lists 6 units and the allowance per 30 days were 2 units. The customer's insulin pharmacy program closed with closure reason "customer discontinued", and its latest insulin refill shipped on a hypothetical 1 June with 60 supply days, so that supply ends on 31 July.

- Next delivery date 1 August: the supply ended before it; Medicare is expected to deny all 6 units.
- Next delivery date 31 July: the supply still runs on that date; Medicare is expected to deny 6 less 2, that is 4 units.
- Same dates, but the closure reason is "changed supplier": Medicare is expected to pay all 6 units and deny none.
- Same closure, but the insulin pharmacy program never shipped an insulin refill: Medicare is expected to deny all 6 units whatever the next delivery date.
- Supply still running on the next delivery date and only 1 unit listed: 1 less 2 falls below zero, so Medicare is expected to deny no unit.
